# HISD adopted budgets: FY2024-25, FY2025-26, FY2026-27

Track: HISD's own **ADOPTED (budgeted)** figures, plus HISD's in-year amendments.

- Audited **ACTUALS** are in [`notes/acfr.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/acfr.md).
- TEA formula data are in [`notes/tea_peims.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/tea_peims.md) and [`data/hisd_sof_trend.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/data/hisd_sof_trend.md).
- Federal and debt material is in [`notes/federal_debt.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/federal_debt.md).

The fiscal year runs July 1 to June 30. "FY25" = 2024-25.

Source files are in [`sources/budget/`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/sources/budget/) (see `SOURCES.md`). Cites take the form (file-abbrev, PDF page). Abbreviations:

Sources for the table above:

- **Revenue, appropriations, and the all-funds gap:** web postings W25/W26/W27 p1. These tie exactly to the GF + Debt Service + Nutrition sums in S25/S26/S27 [calc].
- **GF rows:** S25, S26, S27.
- **Tax rates:** B25 p19, B26 p21, B26 p123, N27.

Notes on the headline table:

- **Only three funds are adopted.** Texas law requires board adoption, by function, only for the General, Debt Service and Nutrition (Food Service) funds (B25 p7, p86). Special Revenue (federal grants), Capital Projects and internal service funds are not in the adopted totals. The Capital Renovation Fund appears "informational only" (B25 p36).
- **Press "$24.5M / $24.6M deficit" for FY27 = GF revenue − GF expenditure.** That is ($24,559,954) (S27).
- **Press "$791,000 draw" for FY27 = the net change after property sales and transfers.** That is ($790,881) (S27).
- **Press "~$2B budget" = GF expenditures.** FY27 GF expenditures are $2.015B; including the $22.2M transfers-out gives $2.037B (WS-May26 slide 13).
- **Budget vs actual:** FY25 GF actual expenditures were $2.25B against a $2.10B adopted and a $2.176B final budget. See [`notes/acfr.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/acfr.md) §2 and §7 below.

### Where the "74% local / 14% state / 12% federal" claim comes from

The press attributes this split to the GF. It is actually HISD's own all-funds chart, which includes the federal grants:

- The split appears as chart 3 in WS-Apr26, "Sources of Revenue."
- It can be reproduced exactly from FY27 all-funds revenue plus the $177.3M of federal grants: local $1,994.5M (73.9%), state $381.7M (14.1%), federal $144.8M + $177.3M (11.9%) [calc].
- On a **General Fund** basis, federal money is only about 1% and state about 18%.

### Reserve benchmarks in HISD's own documents

- **3-month benchmark:**
  - Board policy CE(Local) is a 3-month operating reserve, "~$525M"; the GFOA 2-month standard is "~$350M" (WS-Feb25 p10).
  - WS-Apr26 chart 1 shows a "Fund Balance 3 Months" line of $548M (FY25), $525M (FY26), $518M (FY27). The same chart has "Finance Actual/Projections" of $1,047M (FY24), $748M (FY25), $752M (FY26), $753M (FY27).
  - **Alvarez & Marsal ("A&M") no-action projection** in the same chart: FB of $548M (FY25) and **$252M (FY26)**. Leadership uses this to show the cuts avoided depletion.
- **Months of GF expenditures covered by *total* GF FB, on adopted budgets [calc]:**

  | Budget | Months | Days |
  |---|---|---|
  | FY25 adopted | 4.6 | 139 |
  | FY26 adopted | 4.4 | 135 |
  | FY26 amended | 4.2 | 126 |
  | FY27 adopted | 4.3 | 132 |

  For comparison, FY23's actual $1,127M is about 6.2 months against WS-Apr26's FY23 3-month line of $544M [calc].
  - On an **unassigned-only** basis, the ACFR gives **2.48 months** at 6/30/25 ([`notes/acfr.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/acfr.md)).
- **Press claim "reserves fell ~$450M, ~7 months → ~3 months" (SECONDARY): roughly consistent but loosely defined.**
  - The total FB fall FY23→FY25 is $379M (ACFR). FY23→FY27 adopted is $398M [calc].
  - "~3 months" matches *unassigned* FB or HISD's 3-month line, not total FB.
- **FY27 tax notice M&O fund balance:** $558,903,003 at end of FY26. This is net of the cash needed before the first state aid payment. The I&S balance is $91,832,151 (N27).
- **FY25 policy statements:**
  - "Going forward the district will maintain a minimum of $800 million in the fund balance … four months of district operating costs" (B25 p6).
  - The FY26 assumption was "not dipping below an $800 million fund balance" (WS-Feb25 p15). Both were breached: actual FB was $748M at 6/30/25.

### Deficit drivers HISD itself cited

- **FY25:**
  - End of ESSER: $323.9M of ESSER in FY24 → $0 in FY25 (WS-May24 p24).
  - Property tax revenue fell $351.9M vs FY24's original budget because of state compression and higher homestead exemptions. This was offset by the end of recapture: FY24's original budget had **$326.5M of recapture** and FY25 had $0 (B25 p6, p110).
  - NES expansion to 130 schools.
- **FY26:** the adoption bridge (P26 p13-15).
  - Revenue +$175.4M: Basic Allotment and entitlements +$83.9M; Teacher Retention Allotment +$36.6M; Allotment for Basic Costs +$18.3M; Support Staff Retention +$6.3M; School Safety +$6.6M.
  - Cuts −$122.1M: departments −$29.2M, PUA campuses −$14.1M, NES campuses −$21.5M, one-time −$12.8M, recapture −$44.5M.
  - Additions +$67.8M: teacher pay raise $11.7M, support staff raise $5.8M, SPED staff $13.7M, Pre-K $5.0M, charters/DAEP/JJAEP $10.9M, maintenance tax notes $4.0M, etc.
- **FY27:** the bridge (WS-May26 slide 14).
  - Revenue −$38.4M: enrollment loss −$50M (4,000 students); loss of the "disaster relief tax" pennies −$50M; Teacher Incentive Allotment +$27.5M; property sales +$35M; 1882-partnership pass-through −$24M.
  - Cuts −$124M: central office −$35M, NES decreases −$29M, 1882 partnerships −$19M, school consolidation −$15M, vacancies −$15M, "efficiencies" −$12M, one-time −$6M, overtime −$3M.
  - Increases +$61.5M: PUA/PFP campus pay +$11M; electricity & water +$13.5M; central office salaries +$7.75M and minimum-wage raise +$5M; Future 2 $4.5M; health insurance $4M.
  - **Self-insured health fund:** projected net position −$19.5M (FY26 estimate) and −$5.5M (FY27). This is the reason for the plan consolidation from 7 plans to 4 (WS-May26 slides 41, 48).

### FY26 mid-year status

At March 31 2026, against the Feb amended budget of $2.075B revenue and $2.100B expenditure, actuals were $1.880B revenue and $1.394B expenditure. Projected ending FB was $751,966,507 (WS-Apr26 slide 36, EMF text).

A26-1 added a $46,000,000 "Prior period property value audit" other financing source. That is a one-time item propping up FY26.

## 7. Campus allocation model (how money gets to schools)

### Two systems

| | NES | Non-NES ("PUA", Per-Unit Allocation; renamed EAS, "Earned Autonomy System", May 2026) |
|---|---|---|
| Who builds the budget | Built **centrally** from standardized staffing models (teacher apprentices, learning coaches, SPED aides); principals have little discretion | Principal-built from a per-student formula |
| Formula | Staffing crosswalks (WS-Apr25 pp25-26) | Projected enrollment × attendance (ADA%) × per-unit allocation (WS-May24 p29; WS-Apr25 p13) |

**Year-by-year formula changes:**

- **FY25:** "hold harmless" for enrollment and attendance was eliminated, with loss capped at 12% (B25 p7; WS-May24 p29).
- **FY26:** +$75/student, with 10% of any loss added back (WS-Apr25 p12).
- **FY27:** a new "PPOR" (Per Pupil Operating Revenue) formula (WS-Apr26 slides 42-44; WS-May26 slides 17-33):
  - $1,400 base per student × projected enrollment × ADA;
  - special-population weights aligned to the state's (at-risk, SPED, G/T, CTE, EL, refugee, homeless);
  - teacher salaries funded at actual pay-for-performance levels × 1.15 benefits;
  - magnet allocation;
  - a floor and ceiling: no campus loses more than 1% or gains more than 4% vs its FY26 allocation.
  - NES schools get the same formula plus **+$500 per pupil "academic need"** (WS-May26 slide 20-21 diagram text).

**Autonomy tiers (FY25 book):** Level 4 Separate & Unique magnets (21 schools); Level 3 A/B-rated (57); Level 2 C/D-rated non-NES (41); Level 1 NES (130); special (18); total 267 (B25 p58, image).

## 9. Inconsistencies and errors in HISD's own documents

1. **Tax rate misstatements:**
   - B25's transmittal letter says the budget used "$1.0350 … M&O $0.8683" (p6). The body says $0.8683 total = 0.7016 M&O + 0.1667 I&S (p19, p119).
   - B26's letter says "$1.0450 … M&O $0.8783" (p7 OCR). The body says $0.8783 total (p21, p123).
   - The letters are wrong.
2. **Fund balance typo:** B25 p6 and p91 write the FY24 fund balance as "$1.047 million"; it should read billion.
3. **Unassigned FB repeated:** B25 p91 shows unassigned FB of $590,067,862 for both 6/30/2023 and 6/30/2024. [`notes/acfr.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/acfr.md) confirms this is what the ACFRs report; FY24's drawdown was absorbed by the instructional-reserve assignment.
4. **Recapture FY25:** three HISD figures ($44.5M final budget, $56.97M Dec amendment, $56.9M actual) vs TEA's $49.1M. The FY25 adopted budget assumed $0.
5. **FY26 state FSP:** the narrative says FSP is "approximately $110.5 million" (B26 p88, p113). The revenue comparison table says Foundation Fund $238,160,263 (B26 p114 OCR). The table total ($414.5M) ties to S26, so the narrative likely omits other state programs.
6. **FY26 GF appropriation:** B26 p25 (OCR) shows $2,121,877,295 vs $2,121,893,114 in S26. The $15,819 difference equals function 81.
7. **FY26 Debt Service:** B26 p25 calls $389,749,309 the "Debt Service Fund budget"; that is revenue. Appropriations are $397,003,334.
8. **FY26 beginning FB:** adopted at $799.9M (S26). The book shows $750.4M (B26 p33). The audited figure is $748.1M. The adopted budget overstated starting reserves by about $52M because the FY25 actual deficit (about $297–299M) far exceeded the amended −$247M.
9. **FY25 ADA:** B25 p18 calls 179,592 the ADA; it is HISD's enrollment count.
10. **FY27 May-20 preliminary vs adopted Debt Service:** local revenue was $369.3M in the May 20 preliminary and $383.0M as adopted; ending DS FB moved $159.5M → $173.2M. The GF did not change between the preliminary and adoption.

## 10. Not found or not verified

- **FY27 adopted budget book:** not yet published (FY26's appeared Nov 2025). So FY27 has no object-level, line-item revenue, FTE or school-by-school detail; only function totals (W27, S27) and the workshop decks.
- **FY27 school-by-school allocations, NES vs non-NES per-student:** not published. HISD gives only sample schools (WS-May26 slides 24-33).
- **Special Revenue (federal grant) budget by function, and internal service funds** (health insurance, workers' comp): not adopted or published, except grant planning totals and the health fund statement.
- **Consultant contract amounts** (Alvarez & Marsal, NES curriculum vendors, Dyad/Future 2 vendors): not in budget documents. They would need board agenda items or a contract register.
- **Press articles on each year's adoption:** not fetched (session rate limit). The SECONDARY claims cited are from search snippets only.
- **The 2024 and 2025 tax-rate worksheets** were downloaded but not analyzed.

- **The adopted GF deficit grew every year from FY2021 to FY2024:** −$34.0M, −$82.1M, −$100.8M, −$168.5M. HISD nonetheless ended FY2019-FY2023 with surpluses or break-even.

- FY2023: "$247 million … under recapture, an increase of $34 million" (B23 p8).

### HB6. Inconsistencies and errors in HISD's own FY2019-FY2024 documents

1. **FY2022 adoption date.** W22 says "Date Adopted by Board: June 20, 2021," which was a Sunday. The public-hearing / recommended-budget deck is dated Thursday June 10, 2021 (P22 p1). The posted date is probably wrong; the actual vote date is not confirmed by a primary source here.
2. **FY2019 web posting does not foot.** W19's total appropriations ($2,524,949,501) exceed the sum of its function lines ($2,478,587,728 [calc]) by exactly the GF transfers-out ($46,361,773). Its revenue total includes $84,105,987 of transfers-in ("Other Sources"). The budget book's all-funds page likewise carries the GF at $2,043,345,624, including transfers (B19 p23).
3. **FY2020 has two different adopted totals.** The Jun 27 2019 web posting (W20a) totals $2,423,664,443. The Budget Summary by Function (W20) totals $2,423,526,168. The $138,275 difference equals the public-notice memo line, which W20a added into its total.
4. **The adopted schedules and the ACFR "original budget" column split local revenue differently, though the totals match.** For example:
   - FY2022: property tax $1,895,069,877 / misc. $9,453,620 (S22) vs $1,901,266,733 / $3,256,764 (RSI).
   - FY2024: property tax $1,888,763,457 / investments $39,624,859 / misc. $7,240,000 (S24) vs $1,872,590,384 / $60,537,932 / $2,500,000 (RSI).
   - Similar small reclasses occur in FY2019, FY2021 and FY2023. In FY2020, instruction and FMO differ by ±$1,957.
5. **FY2021 web posting mislabels a line.** The $63,066,742 TIRZ payment is printed on line 96 "Payments to Charter Schools", and line 97 "Payments to TIF" shows $0 (W21). S21 shows it correctly as fn 97.
6. **Adopted budgets understated the starting fund balance, often badly.** Estimated beginning GF FB vs audited prior-year ending [calc]:
   - FY2020: −$236.9M (582.1M vs 819.0M)
   - FY2021: −$89.4M
   - FY2022: −$227.3M
   - FY2023: −$274.7M (−$204.7M counting the $70M "anticipated unspent")
   - FY2024: −$6.5M

   This is the opposite of FY2026, where the adopted budget *over*stated the beginning FB by about $52M (§9 item 8 above).
7. **FY2023 transmittal letter tax-rate error.** It says the rate "was reduced from $1.1331 to $1.0372" (B23 p8). The prior-year rate was $1.0944; $1.1331 is the FY2021 rate. This is the same kind of error as the FY25/FY26 letters (§9 item 1).
8. **FY2024 deck M&O error.** P24 p10: "M&O total tax rate for school year 2023-24 is $0.8090 down from school year 2022-23 of $.8050." The FY2023 M&O rate was $0.8705, and $0.8090 > $0.8050 would not be "down."
9. **FY2021 ADA typo.** B21 p18 prints the ADA as "188,244,477 pupils"; it should read 188,244.477.
10. **FY2023 book relabels a FY2022 actual.** B23 p26 shows the FY2022 actual "Insurance proceeds 21,156,000". The FY2022 ACFR records that $21,156,000 as *issuance of leases* and shows no FY2022 insurance proceeds (FY22 ACFR p.36).
11. **Recapture planning misses.** FY2020 was adopted with $0 and FY2021 with $12.1M; actual was $80.8M and $197.8M. FY2024 was adopted with $326.5M and actual was $0, because of the post-adoption compression and exemption law. Each budget was adopted before the governing legislation or TEA's final values were known.

### HB7. Not found / not retrieved (FY2019-FY2024)

- **FY2020 and FY2024 adopted budget books:** not on HISD's site and not in the Internet Archive (checked the old `filedownload.ashx` captures; list in `_popups/wayback_filedownload_budget_hits.txt`).
- **FY2020 Budget Workshop 7 (Jun 25 2019):** the only Internet Archive captures are truncated at 1 MB (unreadable PDF), so it was not saved.
- **FY2020 recommended-budget presentation:** no capture found. HISD's current site lists recommended-budget presentations only from 2020-21.
- **FY2024 ADA/WADA assumptions, and FY2024 object/FTE detail:** no FY2024 book. The FY2025 book (B25 p22, p39) carries FY24 final-budget object and FTE columns; see §4 and §6.
- **Exact board vote dates other than the TEA postings:** not cross-checked against board minutes. The FY2020 budget (adopted Jun 27 2019) may have followed an earlier failed vote; an Arabic-language HISD press-release file titled "HISD_Board_of_Education_rejects_proposed_budget_for_2019_Arabic_.pdf" appears in the Internet Archive's index of `houstonisd.org/cms/lib2/TX01001591/Centricity/Domain/40261/` (SECONDARY; seen in the index only, not downloaded or read).
- **The 2021-2023 tax-rate calculation worksheets** were downloaded but not analyzed.

### U2. FY2026 enrollment and per-student figures

- TEA's fall 2025 enrolled membership for HISD is **167,793** (TEA 2025-26 budget report header; the campus budget report's campus counts sum to 167,786). TEA's budget and actual reports carry the same fall count for each year (checked for 2019-20 to 2024-25), so this is a count, not a projection.
- TEA's count ran 0.3-0.4% below the ACFR enrollment in FY2023-FY2025 (189,290 vs 189,934; 183,603 vs 184,109; 176,039 vs 176,727).
- FY2026 amended General Fund spending per TEA-counted student: $2,109,408,270 / 167,793 = **$12,571** (no recapture budgeted) [calc]. Excluding TIRZ ($54,247,082): $12,248 [calc].
- FY2027 adopted: $2,015,007,011 / 164,812 (HISD projection, WS-May26 slide 8) = **$12,226** [calc]; excluding TIRZ ($44,698,594): $11,955 [calc].

### U3. Budgets as filed with TEA

TEA publishes each district's adopted budget as filed in PEIMS ("Budgeted Financial Data"). HISD's 2025-26 filing ties to S26: General Fund revenue including TRS on-behalf and other receipts $2,127,033,202 = adopted revenue $2,082,033,202 + property sales and transfers in $45,000,000; total disbursements $2,141,716,843 vs appropriations + transfers out $2,141,717,041 ($198 apart). Details and the per-student comparisons with the state are in [`notes/tea_peims.md`](https://github.com/govspends/us-tx-districts-houston-isd/blob/main/investigations/hisd-funding/notes/tea_peims.md) ("Budgeted data as filed with TEA").
